record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Must every aperiodic infinite word have prefixes of arbitrarily large palindromic length?

evidence.quote: Every aperiodic infinite word has prefixes of arbi- trarily high palindromic length. Next, he put the two following questions:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite word $u$ over a finite alphabet $A$, define the palindromic length $\mathrm{PL}(u)$ to be the smallest integer $k\ge 0$ such that $u$ can be written as a concatenation $u = p_1 p_2 \cdots p_k$ of $k$ palindromes $p_i$ over $A$ (the empty word has palindromic length $0$). An infinite word $w = w_1 w_2 w_3 \cdots \in A^{\mathbb{N}}$ is called ultimately periodic if there exist integers $n_0 \ge 0$ and $p \ge 1$ such that $w_{n+p} = w_n$ for all $n \ge n_0$, and aperiodic otherwise.

Prove or disprove: for every aperiodic infinite word $w$ over a finite alphabet, the set
$$\{\mathrm{PL}(w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n) : n \ge 1\}$$
of palindromic lengths of prefixes of $w$ is unbounded.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Frid, Puzynina and Zamboni, 2013) that the palindromic length of factors—and equivalently of prefixes—of any aperiodic infinite word is unbounded remains open in general. It has been verified in several special cases, including k-power-free words, Sturmian words, and certain automatic words such as the Thue–Morse and Sierpinski words.

status_evidence.title: Palindromic Length of Words with Many Periodic Palindromes
status_evidence.snippet: Frid, Puzynina, and Zamboni conjectured that if w is an infinite word and k is an integer such that PL(u) ≤ k for every factor u of w, then w is ultimately periodic.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated and noted as still open in general, with progress on special cases.

status_evidence.title: Prefix palindromic length of the Thue-Morse word
status_evidence.snippet: Studies prefix palindromic length growth for the Thue-Morse word in support of the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results confirm the conjecture for specific automatic words.

status_evidence.title: On prefix palindromic length of automatic words
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the prefix palindromic length conjecture for automatic words.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture verified for further classes; full case remains open.
